system.reaction: anatase TiO2 + Li2CO3 -> Li2TiO3 (+ CO2) -> Li4Ti5O12; anatase -> rutile in parallel
system.mixing: 5:2 TiO2:Li2CO3 molar ratio, pelletized, loaded in a capillary
system.initiation: sample moved into a pre-heated hot zone; SI Fig. S2 shows it within 50 K of target after 6 s and within 7 K after 10 s (measured at 750 C); t = 0 is insertion into the hot zone. The grey 'Heating' strip in Fig. 3 spans about the first 0.17 min
system.atmosphere_note: not stated in the main text

files.extracted_phase_fractions.csv: Fig. 2: weight % of each phase and Ti-mole fractions on a 0.05 min grid from 0.05 min to the end of each panel (10 min; 9.76 min at 750 C). Columns wt_* sum to 100 by construction (the figure is a normalised stack). tifrac_* are the fractions of Ti in each Ti-bearing phase, computed from wt_* with nominal molar masses (TiO2 79.866, Li2TiO3 109.75, Li4Ti5O12 459.08 g/mol, 1, 1, 5 Ti per formula unit).
files.fig3_482C_li2tio3_relative.csv: Fig. 3: Li2TiO3 at 482 C in arbitrary units (the y axis has no ticks). Values are the fraction of the image height above the x axis, so only the shape and ratios of slopes are meaningful, not absolute amounts. Time 0 to 5 min on a 0.02 min grid. The x-axis row was corrected on Oct 21 (it was taken from the tick-label text row, offsetting every value by about +0.07); slope ratios are unchanged.
files.reconstruction.png: Our own re-plot of the extracted curves for comparison with the printed figures.

checks_done: From t >= 0.35 min the extraction matches the printed figure within 1 wt % (42 spot checks, VERIFICATION.md) and matches an independent read of SI Fig. S1 to 0.2-0.55 wt % RMS.

Maximum Li2TiO3 is 54.2 / 55.4 / 53.7 wt % (700 / 725 / 750 C) against printed maxima of about 54.4 / 55.7 / 55.5-56 wt %; the authors' '~52 wt %' is their approximate figure, so there is no systematic 2 wt % bias from line thickness. The 750 C peak is lost because it lies at 0.28-0.30 min.
Fig. 3 slope ratio, 0.25-0.75 min versus 1-2 min, is 4.1, matching the authors' statement that the fast regime is 4 times the later rate (baseline corrected Oct 21; the ratio is unchanged).
caveats: Weight fractions are normalised to the remaining solid, and CO2 leaves as gas, so wt % has no conserved total. Use the Ti-mole fractions (tifrac_*) for balance checks. Li2CO3 carries no Ti and is tracked in wt % only.

Li2TiO3 is reported by the authors to be Li-deficient (Li2-xTiO3-x), so the nominal molar mass makes the Ti fraction approximate. With nominal formulas the printed fractions imply 0.95-1.02 Li per Ti against 0.8 supplied by the 5:2 mix (VERIFICATION.md); the extraction reproduces the printed values, so this is a property of the published fractions.

Values at t <= 0.3 min are wrong by up to 22 wt % (Li2TiO3) and 14 wt % (Li2CO3): the vertical Li2CO3 label and the converging lines corrupt the stacked figure. The rutile impurity of about 4 wt % present from t = 0 is read as 0, and anatase tails below 1 wt % are cut to 0, so anatase reaches zero too early at 700 and 725 C. Use data/digitized_inputs/chapman2023_sifig_s1/ for early times.

The thin cyan Li2CO3 strip along the top is real but small: SI Fig. S1 plots Li2CO3 at 0.5-0.9 wt % (700 and 750 C) and 1.7-1.9 wt % (725 C) through 600 s. Treating it as zero is defensible because the text says its peaks are indistinguishable after about 30 s.
The 750 C panel's last columns (after about 9.5 min) are an edge artefact.
Boundary lines are 1-2 px thick (5.7 px per wt %), so phase fractions carry roughly 1 wt % of error.
One chemistry, one lab, one capillary geometry. Use as a sanity benchmark, not as evidence about solid-state synthesis in general.
